step2_openloop_cofree.note: open-loop wrk2, attained ~= offered (CO-free true service time). Closed-loop max was CO-inflated AND backwards.

findings: Closed-loop reading was BACKWARDS: CO-free, exeris has the TIGHTEST tail (p99.9 2.36ms, max 25.6ms @30k; still tight at 48k near saturation).
Exeris extreme tail (~22ms p99.999) = the occasional young-GC pause (matches Step 1); benign, heap-independent. No 3am problem in exeris; closed-loop 148ms was CO amplification.

quarkus-hibernate comparable to exeris here (p99.9 4.38ms, max 35.7ms); better than Â§7's co-resident 19.91ms, consistent with Â§7's co-residence thesis.

section7_cross_validation.key_discovery: Â§7 recorded latency_p999_us in every leaf but published p99 only; mining p99.9 strengthens Â§7's own light conclusion.
section7_cross_validation.new_result: At p99.9 exeris is FLAT 1.94-2.60ms while both quarkus arms run 3-8x higher across the ENTIRE ladder (from 6k), whereas Â§7's published p99 shows separation only at 24-30k. Â§7 under-states its own light result.
section7_cross_validation.extends_s7: This run adds a 48k rung (past Â§7's 30k top): exeris p99.9 4.12ms - flatness holds to 84% of its ceiling.
section7_cross_validation.contradicts_this_run: SUPERSEDED: §7 p99.9=12.22ms vs 913/903ms here is a CONFIGURATION difference (§7 quarkus at 0.75x budget heap + 120s window; here matched 256m + 300s), not an outlier in this run.
section7_cross_validation.heavy_context: Â§7 heavy p99.9 @10k: exeris 37.3 (pair-1) / 40.4 (pair-2) vs quarkus-tuned 13.8; hibernate pair-3 99.7 vs pair-2 31.3 reproduces the 'heavier neighbor -> fatter tail' signature. Consistent with Â§7's co-residence reading.

outlier_arithmetic: At 30k rps x 300s = 9M requests, ONE ~1s stall delays every request scheduled during it (~30k = 0.33% > 0.1%), alone driving p99.9 -> ~913ms and p99.99/max -> ~1.0s. Signature of one event in one window; Â§7's 120s windows are less likely to catch it.
caveats: Loopback; fair across stacks, not transferable to real network.
Open-loop rungs sub-saturation (attained ~= offered) => percentiles are true service time; closed-loop max used only as the initiating smoke alarm.

quarkus-tuned ~1s stall is REPRODUCED (n=2) and not database-side, but its CAUSE is unproven and the matched-256m-heap choice is the leading suspect. Do NOT publish as an unqualified 'quarkus has a 1s tail'. Decisive test: quarkus-tuned @30k open-loop with -Xlog:gc,safepoint at 256m vs 768m.

This run is truly single-target (verified: one target-app per run, no co-locator) - the isolated reference Â§7's pairwise harness could not provide. Levels not directly comparable to Â§7's co-resident leaves; ordering and exeris absolutes agree.
